prompt: Build an EnumMap lookup table of shipping rates, quote a parcel from it, and tally shipments per zone. Complete the three methods in ShippingRateTable.
explanation: An EnumMap is created with the key type's class object, new EnumMap<>(Zone.class), and stores its values in an array indexed by ordinal -- that is why it iterates in declaration order and why lookups are so cheap. quoteCents reads the table instead of hard-coding prices in a switch, so a new rate means editing one line. merge(zone, 1, Integer::sum) is the idiomatic counter: it inserts 1 the first time a zone is seen and adds 1 afterwards, which also leaves unseen zones out of the map entirely.
hints: Fill baseRates() with four put calls -- the map is already created for you with new EnumMap<>(Zone.class).
For the surcharge, compute how many grams are above 500 with Math.max(0, weightGrams - 500), then round that up to whole 100s with (over + 99) / 100.
In tally, counts.merge(zone, 1, Integer::sum) handles both the first sighting and every later one; a get/put with a null check works too.
